newsitem.title: USA: Cold wet weather stalls fieldwork in Nebraska.
newsitem.headline: Cold wet weather stalls fieldwork in Nebraska.

text.p: Wet weather in Nebraska stalled fieldwork during the week ended Sunday, and warmer weather is needed to speed crop development, according to the state's weekly agricultural statistics service update.
Temperatures were five to eleven degrees below normal and precipitation was widespread and heavy in some areas, the crop progress report said.

Winter wheat conditions improved from the previous week to three percent excellent, 39 percent good, 45 fair, 12 poor and one very poor. As of Sunday, 94 percent of the wheat had jointed, slightly behind 95 percent a year ago and 99 average.
Sixty percent of the wheat had headed versus 32 percent a year ago and the 57 percent average.
Corn was 90 percent emerged versus 68 percent last week and 83 percent last year. Cutworms were noted in some fields, crop scouts said.
Soybeans were 84 percent planted versus 51 a year ago and the 65 percent average. Fifty-one percent of the crop had emerged versus 23 a year ago and the 35 percent average.
Sorghum planting was delayed, but 77 percent was complete as of Sunday. That pace was far ahead of 42 percent last year and the 55 percent average, according to the report.
Alfalfa was rated six percent excellent, 42 good, 34 fair, 14 poor and four percent very poor. The first cutting was ten days behind normal at five percent harvested.
Topsoil moisture was rated 12 percent surplus, 79 percent adequate and nine percent short.
